title: Prove the sharp global FFT setup constant (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

Prove the sharp FFT setup-sum constant `1017/7` at every integer width `n >= 3`, with equality only at `n=7`.

```diff
- PR3819: finite bound through n = 2^22
+ This result: the same sharp constant for every n >= 3
+ Analytic tail: S < 144 n beta^2 for every n >= 513
```

Claim type: scoped all-width arithmetic proof with an exact finite component. Only `research/fft-setup-global-maximum/` is added. James Reed retains credit for the finite constant and equality case in #3819/#3813; Jose Manuel retains the FFT geometry and setup invoice in #3787 and its predecessor lineage. The new step is the universal tail proof. No predecessor executable or full census was replayed as the deliverable. This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas.

For `beta=ceil(log2 n)`, `q=ceil(n/beta)`, `ell=ceil(log2(2q))`, `r=2^ell` and `p0=2 beta+ell`, the quantity is `S=r(ell+1)p0^2+r p0^3+p0^3`. It is the quadratic majorant of the retained setup invoice, before hidden implementation constants. No new kappa is claimed.

## Evidence

- Before: #3819 explicitly covers only `3 <= n <= 2^22`.
- After: a written ceiling bound and induction cover every `n >= 513`; the exact 510-width prefix attains `1017/7` only at seven.
- Both registered warning-strict, isolated commands pass locally on CPython 3.12.15, normally and with optimization. Each took 0.03 seconds locally. They check independent prefix geometry, 4,087 induction probes, 8,174 tail endpoints, eight rejected invalid widths, three detected formula mutations and rejection of constant 145. Finite tail probes corroborate the written induction rather than supply its universal quantifier.
- Committed-byte/source-history preflight passes at `cb9fd4bb6e9fba8ae3e58e202ac2ba391e514831`. Official export integrity and both direct replays from a read-only Git-free export pass; all six exported files remain unchanged. Every direct run generates a receipt bound to the five package-file hashes.
- The selected-source orientation reports `PASS_RESEARCH_BASELINE_BINDINGS_ONLY`. It is not a selected scientific replay.

Exact reproduction commands from the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/fft-setup-global-maximum
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -I -B research/fft-setup-global-maximum/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -I -O -B research/fft-setup-global-maximum/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/fft-setup-global-maximum --check-source-history
```

The interpreter path is the local reproduction environment; another CPython 3.12 interpreter can replace it. Only the standard library is required.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The result bounds the stated setup expressions. It does not execute the FFT multiplier, establish exact instruction constants, admit a physical caller, discharge retained precision/recovery assumptions, change the selected frontier or prove a complete multiplication theorem. The source uses a different small-width implementation, so the equality at seven concerns this expression rather than a measured production call. The executable probes are capped at 4,096 geometry bits; the written proof has no upper width cutoff. Formal proof-kernel checking, independent human review and separate static type checking are unclaimed. Native, Lean, Docker and full selected cold replays were not run.

## Open next questions

1. Decide whether 144 is the sharp asymptotic upper limit. Start with widths just after power-of-two jumps in `2 ceil(n/beta)` at fixed `beta`. No attaining sequence is supplied here.
2. Bound the unrelaxed invoice using `p0^(8/5)`, with certified real-power comparisons and an analytic tail. Exact instruction constants and caller admission remain separate.

## Related open work

No open PR studying these three FFT setup expressions or their `1017/7` maximum was found in the live body/Discussion overlap snapshot and refreshed targeted searches. The relevant #3819/#3813/#3787 predecessors are merged. Arbitrary diffs and unpublished work are outside the search coverage. The [advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19142745) records the scope and provenance.
